items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: 'You know Baby' which the composer Frank Lewis cooperated with Mary Lou and gave me a few extra bucks to sing.

ctx.x: Then I returned home and decided to take a hot bath to keep from catching a cold, open my bottle of juice and enjoy myself reading my papers until I got sleepy. I took my bath, but when I opened my trumpet case to take my bottle out for a nice big swig, the bottle was empty. What a bring down that was. The cork stopper had come out and the juice had dripped out in the rain. There was not one drop in the bottle and that was one of the worst nights of my life. The liquor stores were closed so I couldn't buy another…

After a few rehearsals with Mary Lou, we recorded for a small company called Asch records. One of the best numbers of the six we recorded was 'Night and Day'. The three of us had put our ideas togeher and Mary Lou wrote the arrangement. Another one I liked very well was 'You know Baby' which the composer Frank Lewis cooperated with Mary Lou and gave me a few extra bucks to sing. But my voice was under-recorded because Asch thought that I was singing too loud. His studio was quite small and so was his sound cabin,…
These recordings were made in August 1944, and later Asch recorded two numbers with the singer Josh White and the line-up was Mary Lou, myself, Eddie Dougherty on drums and Jimmy Butts on bass.
